# Button

## Overview

Button is a pill-shaped, horizontally-laid-out action control with an optional leading icon slot, a text label, and an optional trailing icon slot. It ships in three visual hierarchies (`ghost`, `outline`, `primary`) and four sizes (`default` 48px, `medium` 40px, `small` 36px, `mini` 24px), each with its own padding, icon size, and typography scale. State is a clean four-value axis — `default`, `active`, `disabled`, `error` — captured uniformly across every size in this extraction (no residual `Focus` axis and no size-specific gaps).

**Variant axes.** `hierarchy` (ghost, outline, primary), `size` (default, medium, mini, small), and `state` (default, active, disabled, error) are true Figma variant axes, now named directly (`Variant`, `Size`, `State` — no more anonymous `Property N` labels). `Left icon` and `Right icon` are also true Figma variant axes with real `Yes`/`No` options, decomposed into the boolean props `hasLeadingIcon` / `hasTrailingIcon`. 192 variants were extracted (3 hierarchies × 4 sizes × 4 states × 4 icon-visibility combinations), fully covering the icon-visibility matrix.

**Composition.** The leading/trailing icon child (instance of a component named `squircle`, node `55:8521`) is only present in the tree when its corresponding `Left icon` / `Right icon` variant option is `Yes` — when `No`, the icon child is absent entirely (not merely hidden), confirming these are genuine optional slots. The `Label` text layer is decorative in Figma terms (a raw TEXT node) but is promoted to the parent API as the required `label` string, since it is the button's primary content.

## Known gaps

- **[low] Effect/shadow application is not captured by this extraction.** `resolvedStyles` records two effect styles (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-xs`) but no per-variant node in `colorWalk`/`treeHierarchical` carries an effect-style reference, so this `.md` cannot state which hierarchy/state combinations apply a shadow from this data alone. The already-shipped `V3MiniButton` (and the Small/Medium/Default siblings that mirror its logic) apply `shadow-sm` to `Outline` `default`/`active` only, sourced from an earlier live-node inspection of the Mini pilot — treat that as the current implementation baseline until a future extraction captures effect application per variant.
- **[low] `size="default"` naming collides with the API's actual default value (`"mini"`).** Figma's variant option literally named "default" is the *largest* size tier (48px); the component's actual default variant in the file is `size=mini` (24px). Kept as extracted rather than renamed, to stay Figma-traceable — same call as the prior extraction of this component.
- **[low] Voice/Screen-reader section is inference, not Figma-sourced fact.** `_base.json` carries no dedicated accessibility annotations (no aria layer names, no accessible-name overrides). The Voice section below follows standard button accessibility conventions given the measured `isDisabled` / `isError` props — verify with an accessibility reviewer, especially whether `isError` should trigger any assistive-tech announcement.

Two gaps flagged in the previous extraction of this component are now resolved by this richer extraction and removed from this list:

- Icon-visibility axes are now fully verified — `hasLeadingIcon`/`hasTrailingIcon` are real independent booleans with `Yes`/`No` Figma options, not always-`true`.
- The prior extraction's split between an `Active`-only Mini group and a `Focus`-only Small/Medium/Default group is gone — every size now records a uniform `Default`/`Active`/`Disabled`/`Error` state axis with **identical** hex values per hierarchy×state across all four sizes (spot-checked directly from `colorWalk`), confirming the "color tokens are independent of size" invariant below applies to `active` as well, not only `disabled`/`error`.

## Follow-ups

- **Optional per-child spec.** The leading/trailing icon child (`squircle`, node `55:8521`) is a `COMPONENT_SET` — you may optionally run `create-component-md` on that node to produce its own canonical spec. Not required for this `.md` to be complete or shippable.
- **Effect-application re-extraction candidate.** If the uSpec Extract plugin is updated to walk per-variant effect/shadow application, re-run extraction on this component to confirm (or correct) the Outline `default`/`active`-only shadow behavior currently sourced from the Mini pilot rather than from this `.md`'s own data.

**Cross-section invariants.** The four measured sizes (`default`, `medium`, `mini`, `small`) use identical corner radius (999, pill) and identical `layoutMode`/`HORIZONTAL` structure; only padding, spacing, icon size, and typography scale change. Color tokens are independent of size **and** independent of icon-visibility combination — the same hierarchy × state combination produces identical hex values at every size and at every `Left icon`/`Right icon` combination checked.

## API

### Main table

| Property | Values | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hierarchy` | ghost, outline, primary | false | `primary` | Visual priority / style. Source: Figma `Variant` axis. |
| `size` | default, medium, mini, small | false | `mini` | Source: Figma `Size` axis. Figma's option literally named "default" is the *largest* size tier (48px) — not the API default value. The file's configured default variant uses `mini` (24px). See Known gaps. |
| `label` | string | **true** | – | Button text content. Source: TEXT layer "Label" (placeholder content "Label"). |
| `state` | default, active, disabled, error | false | `default` | Source: Figma `State` axis — a clean four-value variant axis in this extraction (see Known gaps for what changed from the prior extraction). |
| `hasLeadingIcon` | true, false | false | `false` | Source: Figma `Left icon` axis (`Yes`/`No`), fully verified in this extraction — the icon child is structurally absent when `false`, not merely hidden. |
| `hasTrailingIcon` | true, false | false | `false` | Source: Figma `Right icon` axis (`Yes`/`No`), fully verified in this extraction. |

**General notes.** `state`, `hasLeadingIcon`, and `hasTrailingIcon` are independent axes — every combination (3 hierarchies × 4 sizes × 4 states × 4 icon combinations = 192) was extracted, so no mutual-exclusion inference is needed here (unlike the prior extraction's decomposed `isDisabled`/`isError` booleans).

### Sub-components

None. The only conditionally-present child (`squircle`, leading + trailing icon) exposes zero configurable properties in the extracted evidence — see Overview/Composition and Follow-ups.

## Structure

### Anatomy

```
Button (root, HORIZONTAL auto-layout, pill)
├─ Left icon (INSTANCE of squircle, present only when hasLeadingIcon) — leading icon slot
│  └─ Vector
├─ Label (TEXT)
└─ Right icon (INSTANCE of squircle, present only when hasTrailingIcon) — trailing icon slot
   └─ Vector
```

### Root container

| Property | default | medium | mini | small | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| height | 48 | 40 | 24 | 36 | Fixed, not hug. Identical whether icons are present or absent. |
| width sizing | hug | hug | hug | hug | Content-driven (label length + icons + padding) — not a fixed token. |
| padding (vertical, horizontal) | space-12 (12), space-32 (32) | space-8 (8), space-24 (24) | space-2 (2), space-8 (8) | space-2 (2), space-16 (16) | Identical whether icons are present or absent. |
| itemSpacing | space-8 (8) | space-8 (8) | space-6 (6) | space-6 (6) | Gap between leading icon / label / trailing icon. |
| cornerRadius | 999 | 999 | 999 | 999 | Pill shape at every size — literal value, not a variable-mode "shape" collection. |
| layoutMode | HORIZONTAL | HORIZONTAL | HORIZONTAL | HORIZONTAL | |

### Ghost hierarchy root container (distinct height/padding)

| Property | default | medium | mini | small |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| height | 24 | 20 | 16 | 20 |
| padding (vertical, horizontal) | space-0 (0) | space-0 (0) | space-0 (0) | space-0 (0) |
| itemSpacing | space-8 (8) | space-8 (8) | space-6 (6) | space-6 (6) |

### Leading icon / Trailing icon

| Property | default | medium | mini | small | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| icon size (w × h) | 16 × 16 (md) | 16 × 16 (md) | 12 × 12 (sm) | 16 × 16 (md) | Instance of `squircle` (node `55:8521`); identical for leading and trailing at every size, present only when the corresponding `hasLeadingIcon`/`hasTrailingIcon` is true. |

### Label

| Property | default | medium | mini | small |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fontFamily | Noto Sans | Noto Sans | Noto Sans | Noto Sans |
| fontWeight | Medium | Medium | Medium | Medium |
| fontSize | 16 | 14 | 12 | 14 |
| lineHeight | 24 | 20 | 16 | 20 |

## Color

All tokens below are measured from `colorWalk[]` and are independent of `size` — the same hierarchy × state combination produces identical hex values whether the button is `default`, `medium`, `mini`, or `small` (spot-checked for `outline` at `size=small` and `primary` at all four sizes for `state=active`; all four returned the same `#456cb9`). Values are also independent of `hasLeadingIcon`/`hasTrailingIcon`.

### Primary

| Element | default | active | disabled | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background fill | Button/Primary `#244ea2` | Blue/700 (`border/tertiary`) `#456cb9` | Background/Neutral `#e5e5e5` | State/error `#dc2626` |
| Label text | Core/white `#ffffff` | Core/white `#ffffff` | Content/Neutral2 `#404040` | Core/white `#ffffff` |
| Icon stroke | Core/white `#ffffff` | Core/white `#ffffff` | Content/Neutral2 `#404040` | Core/white `#ffffff` |

### Outline

| Element | default | active | disabled | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background fill | Button/Secondary `#ffffff` | Core/black alpha 5% `#000000` (5%) | Background/Neutral `#e5e5e5` | Button/Secondary `#ffffff` (unchanged) |
| Border stroke | Slate/400 (`border/slate`) `#94a3b8` | Neutral/400 (`content/neutral`) `#a3a3a3` | none | Red/500 (`border/extension/error`) `#ef4444` |
| Label text | Content/Primary `#0f172a` | Content/Primary `#0f172a` | Content/Neutral2 `#404040` | State/error `#dc2626` |
| Icon stroke | Content/Primary `#0f172a` | Content/Primary `#0f172a` | Content/Neutral2 `#404040` | State/error `#dc2626` |

### Ghost

| Element | default | active | disabled | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background fill | none (transparent, ~0.01% opacity white — treated as fully transparent) | none (transparent) | none (transparent) | none (transparent) |
| Label text | Content/Extension/Navy `#1d4ed8` | Navy/500 (`border/extension/info`) `#3b82f6` | Content/Neutral `#a3a3a3` | Content/Neutral `#a3a3a3` |
| Icon stroke | Content/Extension/Navy `#1d4ed8` | Navy/500 (`border/extension/info`) `#3b82f6` | Content/Neutral `#a3a3a3` | Content/Neutral `#a3a3a3` |

> Ghost's `disabled` and `error` content colors are identical (`Content/Neutral #a3a3a3`) — confirmed as measured, consistent design intent across all four sizes in this extraction, not a one-off authoring slip (the prior extraction had flagged this as an open question; it now reads as intentional).

### Variable collection

The root fill is bound via the **"Colors semantic"** variable collection (`Light` / `Dark` modes) — e.g. `Button/Primary` resolves to `Blue/800` in both modes in this file. Light/Dark theming is handled automatically by these semantic tokens; it is not a component-level property.

## Voice / Screen reader

> `_base.json` carries no dedicated accessibility annotations for this component (no aria layer names, no accessible-name overrides). The states below follow standard button accessibility conventions given the measured `state` prop — treat as a starting point, not a Figma-sourced fact, and verify with an accessibility reviewer (see Known gaps).

### Focus order

| # | Layer | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Button | The whole control is a single focus stop. |

### Per-state guidance

**default**

| Platform | Behavior |
|---|---|
| VoiceOver | Role: Button. Label: `<label text>`. Traits: Button. Hint: "Double-tap to activate." |
| TalkBack | Role: Button. Label: `<label text>`. State: Clickable. |
| ARIA | `role="button"`; accessible name from visible text or `aria-label`. No `aria-disabled`, no `aria-invalid`. |

**active**

| Platform | Behavior |
|---|---|
| VoiceOver | Label: `<label text>`. Traits: Button, Selected (if modeled as a toggle) or unchanged (if modeled as a transient pressed/focus visual). |
| TalkBack | Label: `<label text>`. State: Clickable; `pressed`/`selected` only if the host app models `active` as a persistent toggle rather than a transient interaction visual. |
| ARIA | `aria-pressed="true"` only if the host app treats `active` as a toggle button; omit for simple action buttons. |

**disabled**

| Platform | Behavior |
|---|---|
| VoiceOver | Label: `<label text>, dimmed`. Traits: Button, Not Enabled. No activation hint announced. |
| TalkBack | Label: `<label text>, disabled`. State: Disabled — removed from the touch-activation traversal. |
| ARIA | `aria-disabled="true"`; excluded from the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) so it is not announced as a focus stop. |

**error**

| Platform | Behavior |
|---|---|
| VoiceOver | Label: `<label text>, error`. Hint: "Double-tap to activate." Error styling is color-only — pair with a text/live-region announcement elsewhere in the flow if the error must be announced. |
| TalkBack | State: Clickable — no distinct TalkBack state for `error`; the red styling alone is not exposed to assistive tech. |
| ARIA | No `aria-invalid` on the button itself (that attribute belongs to form fields). If this button submits an invalid form, pair with the field's own `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` rather than trying to announce error state from the button. |

**Precedence note.** `disabled` suppresses the button's activation hint/state entirely; `error` does not change interactivity, only color and (optionally) an externally-triggered announcement. `active` is mutually exclusive with `disabled`/`error` in the extracted variant matrix (no variant combines them).

- **API ↔ Structure:** `size` (API) drives every row in the Root container / Leading icon / Trailing icon / Label tables (Structure); `hasLeadingIcon`/`hasTrailingIcon` drive whether the corresponding icon row applies at all.
- **API ↔ Color:** `hierarchy` (API) selects the Color section (Primary / Outline / Ghost); `state` selects the column within that section.
- **API ↔ Voice:** `state` has a matching Voice per-state entry; the API's `generalNotes` and the Voice "Precedence note" both describe the same mutual-exclusion behavior.
